method: Actual RainScheduler plans; verified stored spectral-flux attacks at 23.2ms resolution. Energy is relative to each recording; activity threshold is .22. Recurring song-specific note, chord, echo and refrain cells select exact measured attacks, with authored principal/answer weights. Counts include secondary weather and existing physical gestures; maximum bursts use a rolling one-second window. This is a score audit, not listening or YouTube recording verification.
sourceCaveat: Local reference hashes establish which recording the score was measured against. They do not establish that a mapped YouTube upload contains that recording. Mismatched uploads remain held by the player; duration-only and unverified uploads still need recording-identity review.

tracks.title: inhale the Mist
tracks.direction: Begin with fine scattered impacts, then let the rain organize into irregular clusters around the structural change near 2:16. Keep drops small and numerous; use only a few stronger accents. It should feel like pressure gathering in mist, not percussion visualization.

tracks.title: fused (DJ-Kicks)
tracks.direction: Flagship sync candidate. Hold the first ~2 seconds relatively restrained, then let the major transition around 2:06–2:08 cause the rainfall to acquire obvious structure. Use 2–4 drop clusters, selected stronger impacts, and breathing room. Never map every drum hit.

tracks.title: Sun Tickles
tracks.direction: Use small, bright-feeling pinprick impacts in asymmetric groups. Keep the water lively rather than heavy. The earlier 0:24.8 window is the more charming short demo; the ~1:24 window is the higher-contrast machine candidate.

tracks.title: by the rain
tracks.direction: Let the title idea stay implicit. Use fast, narrow clusters and short lulls, with one or two heavier low-frequency accents. Avoid a literal wall of rain and avoid beat-for-drop mapping.

tracks.title: Time to Find Me (AFX Fast Mix)
tracks.direction: Treat the texture as a moving field: showers appear, thin out, then re-form elsewhere. Use asymmetric spatial clusters and deliberate holes. This should feel alien and tactile rather than metronomic.

tracks.title: Pop 4
tracks.direction: Use broad, soft drizzle with slow density swells. Large isolated impacts should be rare. The rain should feel like weather emerging through a continuous field, not like discrete musical notation.

tracks.title: Lusine - Without a Plan
tracks.direction: Use moderate repeating cluster shapes, but vary their spacing and location. Let section changes alter density more than force. Keep enough silence for the ripple interference to read.

tracks.title: memory of a memory
tracks.direction: Favor a late-build choreography: sparse medium drops grow into paired and triplet clusters, then one or two larger soft impacts. Preserve the emotional swell rather than following every transient.

tracks.title: Places Remember Events
tracks.direction: Use a strange, precise rain language: fine irregular clusters, occasional simultaneous impacts in separate regions, and brief silences. The early window is the stronger concise demo; the later window has higher measured contrast.

tracks.title: Sun Arcs (Laraaji Remix)
tracks.direction: Use widely spaced small drops, occasional paired glints, and slow background activity. Let shimmering passages increase spatial spread rather than simply density.

tracks.title: Remember
tracks.direction: The intro is aesthetically interesting, so keep it as an alternate capture. For the stronger full-song passage, use a restrained pulse of small-to-medium impacts with long enough gaps to preserve the melody.

tracks.title: Wilson Tanner - Blush
tracks.direction: Sparse choreography. Use isolated soft impacts and a faint background drizzle only when the energy supports it. Let rings overlap slowly instead of creating busy clusters.

tracks.title: Argento - Sabbia Su Sabbia
tracks.direction: Use tiny granular clusters with broad spatial distribution and low force. Occasional denser moments can resemble grains briefly becoming rain, but keep the surface readable.

tracks.title: Slipping Fingers Through Curls
tracks.direction: Use irregular microdrops, paired events and long gaps. The choreography should feel close and tactile, almost like marks appearing on paper, not like weather.
Use the opening. Almost still water, isolated soft drops, occasional pairs, and substantial breathing room. This track should demonstrate that music sync can be subtle.

tracks.title: Gagánbadibá
tracks.direction: Follow broad rhythmic phrases rather than individual percussion. Use warm, rounded clusters and keep forces moderate. Because the track carries its own cultural/lyrical identity, avoid turning it into a flashy visualizer.

tracks.title: I
tracks.direction: Build layers. Start with a few independent drop streams, then add overlapping cluster patterns as the polyrhythm thickens. Keep individual drops modest so complexity comes from superposition, not force.

tracks.title: birch beer forest
tracks.direction: Use the earlier proven window for the short demo. Mix small irregular impacts with occasional medium accents, letting the rain feel both organic and sequenced. Keep the later high-contrast window as an alternate.

tracks.title: An Unopened Letter
tracks.direction: Use small hand-placed-feeling clusters and soft isolated impacts. Avoid continuous rain. The motion should feel like a sketch becoming animated.

tracks.title: Recovery
tracks.direction: Begin controlled, then increase density and force together through the rise. Use larger impacts sparingly at major phrase arrivals. This can look cinematic without becoming generic.

tracks.title: Continuum 3
tracks.direction: Use graceful density curves, not a beat grid. Let arpeggiated activity produce more small drops while sustained moments pull back. The earlier 1:22.69 window remains a tested visual alternate.

tracks.title: Rider
tracks.direction: Use clean short clusters and sharper spatial changes. Keep one recurring motif in the rain pattern so the choreography feels intentional, then break it at the section transition.

tracks.title: Lights On the Vibe
tracks.direction: Use relaxed, rounded drops and slow cluster entrances. Favor warmth and spacing over technical precision. Good candidate for a long site session rather than a flagship viral clip.

tracks.title: Heal
tracks.direction: Maintain a soft background field and let stronger pulses briefly raise density. Avoid sharp, frequent accents. The rain should feel suspended in a larger atmosphere.

tracks.title: The Dance No. 2
tracks.direction: Use the opening. A few deliberate drops with long decay, occasional paired events, and restrained force. Let the surface remain mostly open.

tracks.title: A Future Untold
tracks.direction: Map musical phrases to broad rain gestures: one larger soft impact can mark a phrase entrance, followed by sparse smaller echoes. Do not chase individual notes.

tracks.title: K-Notes
tracks.direction: One of the clearer high-energy demo candidates. Use compact clusters, quick alternation across the surface, and a few stronger anchors. Keep it playful, not aggressive.

tracks.title: Wildflower Wood
tracks.direction: Use soft scattered rain with occasional slow clusters. Let spatial placement wander naturally across the surface, like weather moving through a landscape.

tracks.title: Bromine (Yamaneko's Irusu Mix)
tracks.direction: Exploit silence. Let drops arrive in small groups, then disappear completely for short stretches. Use faint background texture only when necessary. The absences are part of the choreography.

tracks.title: In Memory
tracks.direction: Use medium-weight impacts and shifting cluster sizes. Let transitions change both density and spatial focus so the surface seems to remember earlier disturbances.

tracks.title: Unknown
tracks.direction: Use broad slow-building rain fields with infrequent stronger impacts. This is more about gradual pressure and release than transient matching.

tracks.title: Da Du Dah (Onome Remix) [feat. Nyron Higor]
tracks.direction: Use loose, human-feeling rhythmic clusters with gentle asymmetry. Keep the choreography warm and flowing; avoid quantizing the rain too tightly.
